newsitem.title: USA: Paxson to sell radio holdings to Clear Channel.
newsitem.headline: Paxson to sell radio holdings to Clear Channel.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp., the largest owner of television stations in the United States, said Monday it agreed to sell its radio holdings to Clear Channel Communications Corp. for $693 million in cash.

Paxson said it would use the proceeds to complete previously announced acquisitions of TV stations. The company, founded with a fortune built on the Home Shopping Network, has said it wants to launch a national television network.

West Palm Beach, Fla.-based Paxson said the tax-advantaged transaction includes its 46 radio stations, six radio news and sports networks and two minor league sports teams, as well as its billboard division. The sale is subject to Federal Communications Commission approval, anti-trust clearance and definitive agreements, the company said.
Forty-two of Paxson's radio stations are in Florida.

"Paxson Communications will use sale proceeds to complete the announced TV station acquisitions," said Paxson Chief Executive Lowell "Bud" Paxson, who in 1991 sold his stake in Home Shopping for $125 million and then began accumulating his network of little-watched UHF television stations, which then became best known for airing paid advertising programming.
"We will now focus and capitalize on our high growth television holdings," Paxson said.
Paxson said it had been holding talks with major broadcast networks, Hollywood movie studios, cable programmers and syndicators "to forge the foundation of a new broadcast television network."
Wall Street applauded the agreement, sending Paxson's shares up 50 cents to $12.875 on the American Stock Exchange. Clear Channel shares were off 62.5 cents at $61.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the purchase price was high, at about 20 times cash flow, but noted the deal offered a rare chance for Clear Channel to add dramatically to its position in Florida. The acquisition gives the San Antonio, Texas-based company 53 radio stations in the state.

"Radio has become all about shelf space and market share and dominating the market share," said Bishop Cheen at First Union Capital Markets in Charlotte, N.C. "Florida is a very attractive market, because of high growth, high population, a very media active market. Paxson has a very attractive Florida platform to enhance Clear Channel's growing platform.
"Clear Channel is willing to pay up because they will increase the profitability dramatically," he added. "They have an excellent radio platform and an excellent management team."
For Paxson the deal means capital to continue its work in television without investing more in its radio empire.

"Paxson is selling because he's got a great value on his asset. He needs capital to finish all the work he wants to do on his television group and on his programming distribution group. And it's very tough to resist the capital that he can get on it," Cheen said.
Paxson said last week that it agreed to acquire the operations of U.S. Travel Channel, a 24-hour cable network, from Landmark Communications Inc. in a $75 million transaction.

In May the company bought New York sports and business station television station WBIS+(Channel 31) from Dow Jones & Co. and ITT Corp. for $257.5 million, giving it a flagship in the nation's largest advertising market just two years after it had tried and failed to buy the station.
Paxson Communications owns 55 television stations in markets serving 58 percent of all U.S. television households, or 56.6 million homes.
